metadata.title: AI Distributed Systems Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary papers and references for 11 distributed-systems primitives: CAP/PACELC, FLP impossibility, Paxos, Raft, vector clocks, CRDTs, idempotency, leases/fencing, quorums, causal consistency, and broadcast protocols

research_papers.name: Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System
research_papers.description: Lamport 1978. Introduced logical clocks (Lamport timestamps) and happens-before relation. Foundation for vector clocks (#5) and causal consistency (#10).

research_papers.name: Impossibility of Distributed Consensus with One Faulty Process
research_papers.description: Fischer, Lynch, and Paterson 1985. Proves no deterministic asynchronous consensus protocol can guarantee both safety and termination with even one crash fault. Foundation for primitive #2 (FLP Impossibility).

research_papers.name: The Part-Time Parliament (Paxos)
research_papers.description: Lamport 1998. Original Paxos consensus protocol. Foundation for primitive #3.

research_papers.name: Towards Robust Distributed Systems (CAP Conjecture)
research_papers.description: Brewer 2000 PODC keynote. Introduced the CAP conjecture. Foundation for primitive #1.

research_papers.name: Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services
research_papers.description: Gilbert and Lynch 2002. Formal proof of the CAP theorem. Foundation for primitive #1.

research_papers.name: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft)
research_papers.description: Ongaro and Ousterhout 2014. Raft consensus algorithm — leader-based, understandable alternative to Paxos. Foundation for primitive #4.

research_papers.name: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types
research_papers.description: Shapiro, Preguica, Baquero, Zawirski 2011. Formal definition of CRDTs (convergent and commutative replicated data types). Foundation for primitive #6.

research_papers.name: Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-Value Store
research_papers.description: DeCandia et al. 2007. Dynamo paper introducing NWR quorums, vector clocks, sloppy quorums, and hinted handoff. Foundation for primitives #5, #9.

research_papers.name: Spanner: Google's Globally Distributed Database
research_papers.description: Corbett et al. 2013. Spanner paper introducing TrueTime-based external consistency across globally distributed transactions. Background for CAP/PACELC (#1) and leases (#8).

research_papers.name: Consistency Tradeoffs in Modern Distributed Database System Design: CAP is Only Part of the Story
research_papers.description: Abadi 2012. Introduced the PACELC model extending CAP to include latency vs. consistency under normal (non-partition) operation. Foundation for primitive #1 (PACELC extension).

research_papers.name: Cassandra: A Decentralized Structured Storage System
research_papers.description: Lakshman and Malik 2010. Cassandra paper describing gossip-based membership, consistent hashing, and tunable consistency. Background for broadcast protocols (#11) and quorums (#9).

research_papers.name: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
research_papers.description: Kleppmann 2017. Comprehensive reference covering replication, partitioning, transactions, consensus, and batch/stream processing. Primary practitioner reference for all 11 primitives.

research_papers.name: The Promise, and Limitations, of Gossip Protocols
research_papers.description: Birman 2007. Analysis of gossip protocol convergence, scalability, and failure modes. Foundation for broadcast protocols (#11).

research_papers.name: Paxos Made Live — An Engineering Perspective
research_papers.description: Chandra, Griesemer, and Redstone 2007. Engineering experience implementing Paxos in Google Chubby; covers multi-Paxos, leader leases, and practical failure modes. Background for primitives #3, #8.

research_papers.name: Shoal++: High Throughput DAG BFT Can Be Fast and Robust!
research_papers.description: Arun, Li, Suri-Payer, Das, Spiegelman. NSDI 2025. DAG-based BFT consensus reducing average commit latency from 10.5 to 4.5 message delays (60% reduction) while matching state-of-the-art DAG throughput. Successor to Bullshark/Shoal. Relevant to primitives #3, #4, #11.

research_papers.name: Basilisk: Using Provenance Invariants to Automate Proofs of Undecidable Protocols
research_papers.description: Zhang, Singh, Chajed, Kapritsos, Parno. OSDI 2025 Best Paper (Jay Lepreau Award). Automates safety proofs for distributed protocols via Provenance Invariants derived by Atomic Sharding static analysis. Applied to 16 protocols. Artifact: github.com/GLaDOS-Michigan/Basilisk. Relevant to primitives #2, #3, #4.

research_papers.name: Smart Casual Verification of the Confidential Consortium Framework
research_papers.description: Howard, Kuppe, Ashton, Chamayou, Crooks. NSDI 2025. Hybrid TLA+ simulation-in-CI approach (Smart Casual Verification) catching 6 consensus bugs (5 safety, 1 liveness) in a production Raft variant without full formal proof. Applicable to any distributed consensus system. arXiv:2406.17455. Relevant to primitives #3, #4, #8.

research_papers.name: Picsou: Enabling Replicated State Machines to Communicate Efficiently
research_papers.description: Frank et al. OSDI 2025. Introduces Cross-Cluster Consistent Broadcast (C3B) and Quorum Acknowledgments (QUACKs) enabling reliable RSM-to-RSM communication with constant metadata overhead and 24x perf improvement over prior approaches. arXiv:2312.11029. Relevant to primitive #11, #3, #4.

research_papers.name: Mako: Speculative Distributed Transactions with Geo-Replication
research_papers.description: Shen, Cui, Sen, Angel, Mu. OSDI 2025. Decouples transaction execution from replication via speculative 2PC with bounded-abort guarantees. 3.66M TPC-C tx/s across 10 geo-replicated shards. Artifact: github.com/makodb/mako. Relevant to primitives #3, #7, #9.

research_papers.name: Design and Modular Verification of Distributed Transactions in MongoDB
research_papers.description: Schultz, Demirbas. PVLDB vol.18 no.12, 2025. Modular TLA+ specification of MongoDB's distributed transaction protocol with automated conformance testing of the C++ implementation. Novel permissiveness analysis. Artifact: github.com/mongodb-labs/vldb25-dist-txns. Relevant to primitives #3, #7, #10.

research_papers.name: Pineapple: Unifying Multi-Paxos and Atomic Shared Registers
research_papers.description: Bantikyan, Zarnstorff, Chou, Tseng, Palmieri. NSDI 2025. Unifies Multi-Paxos and ABD registers via logical timestamps; any node serves reads/writes; >50% median latency reduction vs. Raft in balanced workloads; beats EPaxos tail latency. Relevant to primitives #3, #4.

research_papers.name: Mysticeti: Reaching the Limits of Latency with Uncertified DAGs
research_papers.description: Babel, Chursin, Danezis, Kichidis, Kokoris-Kogias, Koshy, Sonnino, Tian. NDSS 2025 (arXiv:2310.14821). First uncertified DAG BFT protocol to achieve the 3-message-round latency lower bound. WAN commit latency 0.5 s at >200 k TPS; 4× latency reduction on Sui production deployment. Mysticeti-FPC fast path weaves certificates into the DAG without additional round trips. Relevant to primitives #3a, #11.

research_papers.name: Narwhal and Tusk: A DAG-based Mempool and Efficient BFT Consensus
research_papers.description: Danezis, Kokoris-Kogias, Sonnino, Spiegelman. EuroSys 2022 (arXiv:2105.11827). Introduces the DAG-mempool architecture separating reliable transaction dissemination from consensus ordering. Narwhal-HotStuff achieves >130 k TPS vs. 1,800 TPS for standard HotStuff. Foundational predecessor to Bullshark, Shoal, Shoal++, and Mysticeti. Relevant to primitive #3a.

research_papers.name: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
research_papers.description: Zhong, Liu, Chen, Hu, Zhu, Liu, Jin, Zhang. OSDI 2024 (arXiv:2401.09670). Disaggregates LLM prefill (compute-bound) and decode (memory-bandwidth-bound) onto separate GPU pools to independently optimise TTFT and ITL. Demonstrates 7.4× more requests or 12.6× tighter SLO vs. co-located state-of-the-art. Production adoption via vLLM at Meta, LinkedIn, Hugging Face. Artifact: github.com/LLMServe/DistServe. Relevant to primitives #7, #9, #11.

research_papers.name: Pushing the Limit: Verified Performance-Optimal Causally-Consistent Database Transactions
research_papers.description: Ghasemirad, Sprenger, Liu, Multazzu, Basin. arXiv:2411.07049, accepted TACAS 2025. Eiger-PORT+ proves performance-optimal read transactions are achievable under TCCv (Transactional Causal Consistency with convergence), refuting an earlier conjecture that this was impossible. First deductive verification of a complex concurrency control protocol via model refinement. Relevant to primitive #10.

research_papers.name: In Link We Trust: BFT at the Speed of CFT using Switches
research_papers.description: Zeno, Ben-David, Silberstein (Technion). NSDI 2026, pp. 1431-1452. SwitchBFT uses packet source authentication to drop cryptographic signatures on the fault-free path and programmable switches to enforce agreement and verify safety, reaching the speed of NOPaxos (in-switch CFT). Data-centre trusted-network assumption only; does not transfer to WAN or public-validator settings. Relevant to primitives #3, #3a.

research_papers.name: Jetpack: Consensus Made Generally Fast
research_papers.description: Tang, Zhang, Shen (Stony Brook), Shi (DatenLord), Mu (Stony Brook). OSDI 2026. Plugin framework retrofitting a 1-RTT fast path onto existing consensus protocols by racing fast and original paths while forcing the original path to honour the committed decision. Up to 60% average commit-latency reduction across six consensus systems over 10 AWS datacentres. Names the 'view change hazard': stable-operation promises can become invalid after leader elections. Relevant to primitives #3, #4.

research_papers.name: Equal Opportunity: A Correctness Condition for Ordered Consensus
research_papers.description: Zhang, Ni, Basu, Cohen, Yin, Alvisi, van Renesse, Chen, Zhou (Cornell / UW / UCSB / Microsoft Research). OSDI 2026. Formalises ordering fairness as a correctness condition distinct from agreement and liveness; introduces the Secret Random Oracle (trusted-hardware and threshold-VRF constructions) and Pompe-SRO, mitigating front-running and sandwich attacks at moderate latency cost. Relevant to primitives #3, #3a, #11.

research_papers.name: Acumen: Encrypted Real-Time Collaboration with Strong Snapshot Consistency
research_papers.description: OSDI 2026. First CRDT-based system providing strong snapshot consistency under end-to-end encryption: untrusted users create verifiable snapshots to invite collaborators without revealing prior edit history. Also provides confidentiality, integrity, and fork-causal consistency via cryptographic accumulators and a secure garbage-collection mechanism. Evaluated at 25 concurrent typists. Relevant to primitives #6, #10.

research_papers.name: AWS Post-Event Summary: Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in US-EAST-1 (October 20, 2025)
research_papers.description: Official AWS post-event summary. Latent race condition between two concurrent DynamoDB DNS Enactor processes produced an empty DNS record for the regional endpoint; recovery then caused congestive collapse in EC2 lease re-establishment and a backlog of network state propagation, cascading to NLB, Lambda, ECS, EKS, STS, Redshift and 100+ services. Canonical worked example of a control-plane automation failure rather than an algorithmic consensus failure. Relevant to the operational-triage sections and primitives #8, #11.

research_papers.name: Jepsen: MariaDB Galera Cluster 12.1.2
research_papers.description: Kingsbury, 2026-03-16. Tested 12.1.2 through 12.2.2. Under MariaDB's recommended innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=0, committed transactions were lost on coordinated crashes; setting it to 1 reduced but did not eliminate loss. Also found lost update (P4) and stale reads in healthy clusters against a claimed isolation 'between Serializable and Repeatable Read'. Reference case for the trap of trusting vendor-recommended configuration as a durability guarantee. Relevant to primitives #1, #9, #10.

research_papers.name: Jepsen: TigerBeetle 0.16.11
research_papers.description: Kingsbury, 2025-06-06. Tested 0.16.11 through 0.16.30. Only two safety issues found; exceptional resilience to disk corruption across every replica; Strong Serializability upheld. Positive reference case for systems built around deterministic simulation testing from the start. TigerBeetle's companion post 'Fuzzer Blind Spots (Meet Jepsen!)' documents what in-house fuzzing missed. Relevant to the testing section and primitives #4, #9.

research_papers.name: Automerge 3.0 Release Notes
research_papers.description: July 2025. Re-implementation using the columnar compression format in memory as well as on disk: >10x memory reduction (Moby Dick document 700MB to 1.3MB) and long-history load times cut from hours to seconds. Automerge 2 file format retained; the deprecated Text class was removed (strings collaborative by default) and RawString renamed ImmutableString, so upgrading is a migration. Relevant to primitive #6.

research_papers.name: CoAgent: Concurrency Control for Multi-Agent Systems
research_papers.description: Lyu, Zhang, Wu, Wei, Chen. arXiv:2606.15376, June 2026 preprint (not peer-reviewed; cited for its diagnosis rather than as a settled result). Argues 2PL and OCC fit agent workloads badly because agent transactions span long inference, have broad opaque read sets, and write unbuffered through tools. Proposes MTPO (Monotonic Trajectory Pre-Order): fix a serialization order at launch, serve order-filtered reads, apply writes speculatively in place over undoable tools. Reports within 5% of serial correctness at 1.4x speedup. Relevant to primitives #6, #7, #10.
